correctness.rationale: From the actual RESULT.md at pinned commit, independent disk and uniform-height coordinates give M_p(q)=q^{-p/3} E[(T²+q²U²)^{p/2}]. For p>0 the pointwise log-sum-exp in s=log q is strictly convex and coercive, hence unique global q_p. Independent differentiation of M4 gives 4q^4+5q²−50=0 and M2 gives q²=3. Near T=2,U=1, density exponents 3/2 and 1 yield Laplace p^{-9/2} with prefactor √(2/π)(4+q²)^{9/2}/q^4. Its log-gradient at q=√2 is −√2/2 and leading log-Lp curvature is 2/9, giving q_p=√2+9√2/(4p)+O(p^{-2}). Differentiated uniform boundary remainders are asserted with a plausible endpoint-neighborhood and exponential-tail dominated expansion; numerical values do not prove it.
residual_risks: Laplace expansion needs locally uniform first derivative; supported by smooth local expansions but not formal computer proof.
